title: Caramel d’arachide (Caramelised Peanuts)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Equal glasses of unskinned peanuts and sugar with half a glass of water: sugar dissolved on low heat, peanuts added on medium heat until thick and viscous, then stirred until dry.
longDesc: p. 50 of the October 2023 recipe book: 1 glass unskinned peanuts, 1 glass sugar, ½ glass water (glass size not printed). Sugar dissolves in the water on low heat; the peanuts are added; it cooks on medium heat, stirring from time to time; when thick and viscous it is stirred continuously until it ‘dries’; poured into a dish and cooled. The peanuts end up coated with a light layer of pink caramel, the colour coming from the skins. The page says quantities are proportional for all the ingredients, and that to make the grains stick together the sugar should be increased and left to melt after caramelisation. Times are not printed.
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the water on low heat.
Add the peanuts and cook on medium heat, stirring from time to time.
When the mixture is thick and viscous, stir continuously until it is dry.
Pour into a dish and cool.
chefTips: The printed cues: ‘thick and viscous’, then ‘dry’, with a light pink caramel coating.
The pink colour comes from the peanut skins, per the page.
commonMistakes: Using peeled peanuts and expecting the pink colour.
servedWith: Served as an aperitif or snack
healthBenefits: Peanuts add protein; sugar is a major share of the weight.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe. The page calls it a crunchy, simple aperitif.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Caramel d’arachide ou arachide caramélisée’ (p. 50). Authors as printed: ‘Tata Ngome et al.’ (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré; ReSI-NoC project); October 2023 (V1), © 2024, CC BY 4.0. Yield not printed for any recipe in the book. Servings 6, prep, rest and cook are placeholders. TWO-PASS.
